#1 @user_118: I am using the Oticon Intent 1. my phones are a Galaxy S25 Ultra and a ZFOLD 7. Both phones support LE AUDIO. After connecting the hearing aids via Bluetooth, I can choose between the LE AUDIO hearing aids and the ASHA hearing aids. It is great that I can choose to use either the phone micophone or the hearing aid micophone for calls. However, even if I select the ‘phone microphone’, the ‘hearing aid microphone’ still works. I think this is likely due to hands-free calling. As a result, the other person cannot understand my voice well durring calls. I only want to use the ‘phone microphone’ during calls. How can i do this? I do not want to use the ‘hearing aid microphone’.

#7 @user_118: I also made the same settings, but it doesn’t work. To “really” get the phone microphone to work, First, set the “Microphone for calls” to “Hearing Aid Microphone.” Then, when a call starts and a notification appears in the top pop-up asking “Do you want to switch to the phone microphone?”, you must press the “YES” button for the phone microphone to function properly.

#8 @user_118: I always use Samsung’s default phone app. However, surprisingly, the error I mentioned only appears in the Samsung phone app. The symptoms do not appear in Kakao Phone or LINE Phone.

#9 @user_118: I am also using a Galaxy Z Fold 7 running One UI 8.5. However, just as I mentioned, only the hearing aid microphone works. After researching for a few days, I found a way to use the phone’s microphone. Go to Bluetooth Settings - Hearing Aid Settings - ‘Microphone for calls’ - ‘Hearing Aid Microphone’. Set it up this way first. Then, when a call starts, a pop-up notification appears at the top as follows: “Would you like to switch to the phone microphone?” If you press “YES,” the phone microphone “really” works. The hearing aid microphone does not work. However, this is a temporary solution. I wish the microphone could work as configured in the settings menu.

#5 @user_112: @user_118 I have Resound Vivia HA’s and a Galaxy A36 and, until recently, it behaved as I think you are describing. On calls, the option to “Select Phone Mic” would appear and could be selected, but the phone wouldn’t actually switch. The hearing aid mic would remain the active mic which was unsatisfactory. #10 @user_112: My settings for The Galaxy A36 5G, BT 5.4, Android 16, One UI 8.5 Hearing Aids On (out of charger) Tap Settings Tap Connections Tap Bluetooth Tap Settings (gear symbol) for Hearing Aids Tap Default Settings for Calls Select “Phone Microphone” Select Off for “Get notifications to Change…” Select “Done” Phone now displays after step 4 Default microphone for calls: ”Phone microphone” The phone stays in this mode. On calls, the phone mic is used by default, and the audio is streamed to the hearing aids. No switching is required. Edit: I think new to One UI 8.5, at the bottom of the hearing aid settings page there is now a selection for “Hearing aid type” Mine is in the “LE Audio” mode vs a selectable “ASHA” type.

#4 @luogangan: Your callers are right, and your instinct about hands free calling is too. Factory side note on why this matters so much: an ear level mic is close to the worst possible place to pick up your own voice. It’s far from your mouth, it hears the room, and on top of that the call link often narrows the audio bandwidth. Phone mic near your face wins every time. On the fix, one distinction usually explains the “setting doesn’t stick” mystery. The default microphone toggle governs regular cellular calls. App calls, WhatsApp, Teams, KakaoTalk and friends, request their own audio route and will happily grab the hearing aid mic again. So test a plain phone call first. If the phone mic holds there but fails inside apps, it’s the apps, and inside each app’s call screen you can usually switch the audio source to Phone during the call. Two more things worth checking on Samsung. That default mic choice sometimes resets after the aids reconnect, so re check it after a day of use before trusting it. And if all else fails, switching the in call output from your aids to Phone mid call forces both directions off the aids at once, blunt but reliable.

The reason it won't stick is worth knowing, because it means you didn't do anything wrong. A setting that sits there and does nothing is more annoying than not having it at all.

Under LE Audio a call isn't one stream, it's a configuration both ends agree on at the moment the call starts. The phone can only offer downlink to the aids plus uplink from the phone mic if your aids advertise that they're able to run that way. If the Intent only offers the two way conversational configuration, the phone has no legal option to honour your preference, so it either ignores it or asks you at call time. That popup isn't a workaround you stumbled onto, it's the phone falling back to a second configuration because the first one wasn't on offer.

Which fits what Jay is seeing. Same One UI, same version, different aids, different behaviour. That's the tell that this sits on the aid side rather than with Samsung.

A couple of things you can do rather than wait on anyone.

Borrow the one step of Jay's path you haven't tried yet: set Phone Microphone, then turn off get notifications to change, then make a call. If the phone mic holds with the popup gone, your setting was fine all along and the notification flow was eating it. If it falls back to the aid mics, you've proved the Intent doesn't offer that configuration and you can stop chasing settings altogether. Either answer ends the guessing, and that's worth more than another week of combinations.

If pressing YES on every call is wearing you down meanwhile, ASHA hands you the phone mic by force, because ASHA carries no microphone at all. You give up some quality for it, and I know the advice here has been to stay on LE, so treat it as somewhere to switch for a call that matters rather than somewhere to live.

Either way it's worth putting to Oticon rather than Samsung: does Intent firmware advertise a phone mic conversational configuration at all. If it doesn't, no amount of settings work gets you there and it's a firmware item.

I don't have Intent's firmware in front of me, so take that as the factory side reading of the symptom rather than something I can confirm.
